context.process_name: Deemed Contributions, Fee Waivers & Special Profits
context.objective: Document how we carry out Deemed Contributions, Fee Waivers & Special Profits, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: Honestly I do not know what kicks the whole thing off, that is another team and it happens before it reaches me. My part starts in the middle: the management-fee preparer hands me the approved management-fee calculation for the period or event, and I, as the fund administration preparer, pick it up from there. From that calculation I obtain the gross management fee, the applicable offsets, the waiver amount, the net fee and the member allocation.
What do you do with the gross fee, offsets, waiver, net fee, and member allocation once you’ve obtained them?

I validate the handoff. I confirm the period, the entity, the effective dates and that I have the approved version. Then I confirm the waiver amount agrees to the method or schedule in the arrangement, and I reconcile the current-period input to the cumulative fee-waiver tracking in the ICC roll-forward, which is an Excel schedule. The check is that the waiver input traces to the approved fee calculation and does not exceed the governing arrangement. If there is an unexplained fee or waiver difference I return it to the management-fee preparer or the client. If it is fine, the result is the approved current-period waived-fee input, and then I record the deemed contribution.
How do you record the deemed contribution after the waived-fee input is approved?

I need the approved waived-fee amount and the eligible-member population. I calculate the approved deemed contribution by member using the governing arrangement, add it to that member's life-to-date ICC roll-forward, and reduce the applicable waiver-funded unfunded commitment as approved. Then I update the GP capital-account support and the accounting workpapers, keeping the cash-funded and waiver-funded components separately visible. The accounting or Fund Team posts the entry where applicable. The check is that the current deemed contribution equals the approved waived-fee treatment and that cumulative funded plus unfunded reconciles to the commitment. One gap: the accounting entry and the exact offset accounts are not specified, so I have to obtain approved accounting direction; who approves the journal entry I do not know. After that comes capital-call treatment.
How does the governing arrangement determine each eligible member’s deemed contribution from the approved waived-fee amount?

There is no single formula I can give you. It is fund-specific: the waiver amount is either specified by the LPA, based on a predetermined fixed schedule, or waived first and later trued up to the final amount, and I apply whichever one is documented for that fund. Beyond that I do not know a general rule. What I can describe is the next step, capital-call treatment, which I coordinate with the capital-call event preparer when a call includes a waiver-funded member. I identify the member's total allocation for the event, separate the amount satisfied through deemed or waiver funding from the cash due, keep the member in the correct population while preventing a cash call for the waiver portion, update the allocation file and notice data in the capital call workbook to show the funding source, and reconcile the event results to the ICC roll-forward and the GP unfunded schedule. The check is no duplicate funding: cash due plus deemed or waiver amount equals the approved member allocation. If the notice disclosure or call treatment is unclear I escalate to the client or their advisor; the exact notice wording is not settled.
How does the capital-call event preparer know the updated allocation file and notice data are ready to use?

I do not know of a defined signal for that; we coordinate on it and the output is the approved cash-versus-waiver event allocation, with the client confirming, but how the handover is flagged is not written down as far as I know. The last thing I do is confirm the special-profits method and the available-income condition, together with the client's tax or legal advisor and with client approval. I identify the fund's selected special-profits methodology and timing, obtain the governing definition of available income, determine the member and GP population and the target economic adjustment, and confirm whether the current period or event satisfies the available-income condition. Then written advisor and client approval is needed before anything is calculated or any accounting entry is recorded. In practice this is on hold: the formula and method are not specified, so I hold and obtain advisor direction. If available income is insufficient, no special profits are shifted and we follow client direction. The actual calculation and recording of special profits, and how the period is closed out, is someone else and I do not know how it ends.
What information do you use to determine whether the period or event meets the available-income condition?
